messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: realtime.slo_streaming.p99 breached threshold (tripped at 1200ms -> current 1850ms). impact: ~4% of live streams experiencing stalls. alert rule: realtime-stream-p99 > 1s for 5m. trigger: 2481112219

sara (oncall): acked. looking at dashboard now — thanks bot. first quick checks: is this global or region-specific?

mike_infra: I'm seeing spike from us-west-2 primarily. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/streams/realtime?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2 shows p99 jump at 22:16 UTC. CPU on inference-nodes looks normal, but GPU util jumped on pool-g2-large-3.

raj_ml: did we auto-fallback to the lower-accuracy quantized model? routing logs look like requests were pinned to v2.0 for some customers.

lina_support: a couple enterprise customers opened chats reporting partial transcripts stalling. nothing yet flagged as data loss.

alex_sre: paste of quick queries i'm running:
```
# check active streams and stalls count
select count(*) from stream_events where event_type='stall' and region='us-west-2' and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes';
# check prod pods restarts
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=inference -o wide
```

alex_sre: result: stalls ~420 in last 10m (baseline ~20). no pod restarts.

sara (oncall): ok next steps — mitigate customer impact first, then root cause. mike can you open a capacity bump for us-west-2? enable burst nodes and push routing to warm fallback pool.

mike_infra: bump requested, starting scale up for dedicated pool (expected 90s). also enabling temporary routing fallback to v1.8-quant (lower mem but faster decode) for non-enterprise customers. command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --service realtime --region us-west-2 --policy fallback:v1.8-quant --targets non-enterprise
```

mike_infra: applied. rolling config out.

raj_ml: quick check on KV cache hit rates — looks like a cache churn spike coincident with increased sequence lengths. p95 sequence length increased from 150 -> 520 for some customers. that could cause KV cache thrashing and tail regen cost.

lina_support: enterprise customers pinned to v2.0 — do we want to reach out and enable degraded routing for affected enterprise tenants?

sara (oncall): yes, prioritize reducing stalls. liaise with account owners on temporary degraded mode, mark as opt-in for safety. lina, handle comms. raj, can you throttle max_inflight_tokens for v2.0 per-tenant?

raj_ml: adding a per-tenant cap via rollout flag now. snippet:
```
experimentctl set realtime.v2.flow_control --tenant affected-corp --max_inflight_tokens 256
```
applied to 3 tenants so far. monitoring impact.

alex_sre: on-call checklist:
- verify autoscale exercised (in progress)
- watch tail latency dashboards (https://monitoring.internal/redwood/tail-latency)
- collect a 5-min packet capture of request distrib and model-kv metrics

mike_infra: autoscale completed +2 nodes, routing fallback finished. preliminary drops in p95 but p99 still high (~1.2s).

sara (oncall): good. is streaming stall root cause likely model compute or network egress? can we get a sample trace?

alex_sre: uploading a trace to the incident storage: s3://incidents/2481112222/trace-22-16.json (redacted). shows long waits in decode_gpu_kernel on a subset of requests — queueing on GPU.

raj_ml: that matches sequence-length observation; larger sequence lengths blow up attention compute. for streaming we also have more KV misses which trigger recompute. options: 1) force quantized path for heavy requests (already used for non-enterprise), 2) enable prefix caching eviction policy tweak, 3) smooth ramp by enforcing per-request token cap.

lina_support: enterprise customers are ok with a temporary degraded mode if it means stable streams. I've messaged the two main POCs and got verbal approval for degraded routing for one tenant.

sara (oncall): okay implement ridge mitigation: keep autoscale + fallback for non-enterprise + per-tenant cap for affected enterprise (opt-in). also create mitigations note in incident doc. alex, create an incident-forward ticket and tag eng-runtime and ml.

alex_sre: done. incident ticket: INC-24811122 in tracker. I've pinned current metrics and attached traces.

mike_infra: after mitigations, stalls dropped to ~35 in last 5m, p99 at 940ms. continuing to watch.

raj_ml: starting a deeper investigation: reproducer job queued to simulate long sequences on g2 pool. will run 1h test and collect kernel-level timings.

sara (oncall): great. keep updates here. next update in 15m or sooner if customer impact changes. I'll keep paging suppressed for this incident while we're actively mitigating (:no_bell:).

lina_support: logging customer comms: 2 customers notified via workspace; support inbox updated.

alex_sre: follow-ups created:
- 런: adjust cache eviction policy and test impact (eng-runtime)
- 런: add early-detect alert for rapid sequence-length shifts (observability)
- 런: evaluate per-tenant default token cap vs throughput tradeoffs (ml infra)

sara (oncall): thanks team. closing active mitigation loop, leaving postmortem to eng-runtime + ml. will hand off to oncall rotation for long-term RCA.

incident-bot: Incident incident-24811122 status updated -> mitigated. pages suppressed.

sara (oncall): handoff: handing to alex_sre for overnight watch. alex you have the keys.

alex_sre: taking handoff. will escalate if p99 > 1.1s again. monitoring dashboards + alerts set.
